extracted.intended_audience: Users, implementers, and readers of Knuth's TeX and METAFONT books; people who report bugs or maintain TeX/METAFONT sources
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for the Knuth 'Computers & Typesetting' volumes, their sources, errata handling, distribution restrictions, and how to report bugs or copyright infringements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete documentation via the five volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: These volumes form the complete documentation of the TeX and METAFONT systems for digital typography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Volume roles: Volume A / The TeXbook (user manual/reference), Volume B / TeX: The Program (source code), Volume C / The METAFONTbook (user manual/reference), Volume D / METAFONT: The Program (source code), Volume E / Computer Modern Typefaces (METAFONT definitions). Volumes A and C are paperback user manuals; B and D contain source code written with literate programming; Volume E defines ~500 characters with METAFONT and shows how to vary fonts by changing parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult CTAN for up-to-date sources and errata
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections to old printings can be found in the Comprehensive TeX Archive Network (CTAN). The complete electronic sources and errata are available in CTAN subdirectories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key CTAN paths and files: systems/knuth/dist/errata (errata.tex, PDF of typeset errata), systems/knuth/dist/tex/texbook.tex (TeXbook source), systems/knuth/dist/mf/mfbook.tex (METAFONTbook source), systems/knuth/dist/tex/tex.web and systems/knuth/dist/mf/mf.web (program sources), fonts/cm/mf/*.mf (Computer Modern font sources). Files tex82.bug, mf84.bug, cm85.bug contain records of past changes. Use these canonical files for authoritative, up-to-date information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errata lists and change logs are authoritative
rubrics_metrics.description: The official errata lists and the .bug files contain historical and recent corrections to TeX, METAFONT, and Computer Modern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Errata are organized (errata.one ... errata.twelve) for older printings and errata.tex for recent changes. For a detailed history see chapters referenced in Knuth's other books and TUGboat 'tuneup' articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bug-reporting channel and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not send purported error reports directly to Knuth; send them to tex-k@tug.org for vetting and redirection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you prefer private submission, send mail to karl@freefriends.org. Submit only if you are quite sure the error is real — reports will be vetted by volunteers and, once certified, put into a queue for Knuth to review during periodic maintenance intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit only well‑validated error reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Although everyone wants the systems to be correct, people should submit reports only when quite sure the error is real.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vetted reports are queued for Knuth's periodic review; gratuitous or uncertain reports burden maintainers. The page explicitly requests caution because volunteers handling reports are busy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reward policy for discovered bugs
rubrics_metrics.description: Monetary rewards are offered for discovered and verified bugs in the programs and in the books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you find a previously undiscovered bug in the TeX or METAFONT programs, Knuth will reward you with 0x$80.00 ($327.68). Corrections to errors in The TeXbook or The METAFONTbook are worth 0x$1.00 ($2.56), as in his other books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Version-number convention as an indicator of convergence
rubrics_metrics.description: The TeX and METAFONT version numbers approach mathematical constants as an indication of convergence toward an error-free state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current versions cited: TeX 3.141592653 (plain.tex 3.1415926535); METAFONT 2.71828182 (plain.mf 2.71). Knuth's 'last will and testament' is that the version numbers ultimately become π and e respectively, at which point the systems are 'completely error-free by definition.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance cadence for source corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Knuth periodically reviews accumulated, vetted bug reports at multi-year intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically he reviewed in 1992, 1993, 1995, 1998, 2002, 2007, 2013, and 2020; he intends future reviews at the ends of years 2028, 2037, 2047, etc. Intervals between reviews are increasing as the systems converge toward stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and permitted use of texbook.tex
rubrics_metrics.description: The texbook.tex source file is copyrighted and distributed only to show examples of TeX input, not for creating books like The TeXbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The source begins with explicit comments and a loop that produces an error to prevent TeXing: '% The file is distributed only for people to see its examples of TeX input, not for use in the preparation of books like The TeXbook.' Permission for other uses must be obtained in writing from the copyright holder and the publisher. If you see illicit PDF copies of the books, report them to board@tug.org so the community can act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not redistribute or reproduce illicit copies; report infringements
rubrics_metrics.description: Illicit postings of PDF copies of Knuth's books are violations of the distribution restrictions and should be reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you encounter illegal copies online, send a note to board@tug.org for community/legal action. The page chastises those who ignore the explicit restrictions in texbook.tex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source transparency and learnability via literate programming
rubrics_metrics.description: Knuth published the complete sources for TeX, METAFONT, and Computer Modern, using the literate programming methodology to make the code clear and teachable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Volumes B and D present program source code in a literate-programming style ('Never before has a computer program of this size been spelled out so clearly and completely'). Volume E's METAFONT programs reveal techniques and allow readers to create personal variations and special symbols by changing parameters or using examples as models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check printing details for corrected/updated editions
rubrics_metrics.description: Different printings incorporate various corrections and updates; consult printing numbers and special editions for the most accurate copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Millennium and Jubilee editions and later printings include numerous corrections and refinements. The page lists printing numbers for new printings (e.g., Volume A 23rd printing for Jubilee, etc.) and explains that reprintings made from originals or reconstructed camera negatives impacted quality and corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community resources: contact TUG and local user groups
rubrics_metrics.description: The TeX Users Group (TUG) and local user groups are the best current sources of information about TeX and METAFONT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An up-to-date list of usergroups is at http://tug.org/usergroups.html. General contact email: board@tug.org. Use these community channels for information, support, and coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep fonts and printings current
rubrics_metrics.description: If fonts you use are old, change them — newer printings and electronic methods yield better typography and more lasting quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page emphasizes that updated printings (after the loss of original films) were produced with more durable technology and include many small improvements; updating fonts and using current sources improves output quality.
